podcast.title: Acquisition of "Love Is Strange" Share
podcast.body: According to Bo Diddley, he sold his share in the song "Love Is Strange" to Sylvia sometime in the early 1960s, a move that aligns with her reputation for making "very wise business decisions." "According to Deadly, he also later sold his own share in the song to Sylvia, sometime in the early 60s. This may well be the case, because Sylvia Van Tapool went on to become a very, very successful businessman, who made a lot of very wise business decisions."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Business Acumen and Ambition
podcast.body: Sylvia possessed a "razor-sharp business mind" and a "huge amount of ambition and a desire for stardom," contrasting sharply with Mickey Baker's more private and studious nature. "Sylvia had a razor-sharp business mind, a huge amount of ambition and a desire for stardom."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 49: "Love is Strange" by Mickey and Sylvia

podcast.title: Day Job as a Typist
podcast.body: By the age of 20, Sylvia was working as a typist, struggling to make a living as a singer despite taking guitar lessons from Mickey Baker and becoming "pretty good." "By the time she was 20, Sylvia was holding down a day job as a typist, trying and failing to earn enough money to live on as a singer, but she'd been taking guitar lessons from Mickey Baker and had got pretty good."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Early Career as "Little Sylvia"
podcast.body: Sylvia began her recording career at the age of 13, using the stage name "Little Sylvia," inspired by Little Esther, who also recorded for Savoy Records. "Sylvia was only 13 when she started her career, using the name Little Sylvia, inspired by Little Esther, who like her was making records for Savoy records."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 49: "Love is Strange" by Mickey and Sylvia

podcast.title: Founding All Platinum Records
podcast.body: After the duo with Mickey Baker split, Sylvia took a few years off to have children before establishing her own record label, All Platinum. For this label, she wrote and produced a number of proto-disco hits for other artists. "After a few years off to have kids after the duos split up, she set up her own record label, All Platinum."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 49: "Love is Strange" by Mickey and Sylvia

podcast.title: Lead Guitar and Backing Vocals for Ike & Tina Turner
podcast.body: On Ike & Tina Turner's hit "It's Gonna Work Out Fine," Sylvia played the lead guitar part and joined The Ikettes on backing vocals, making the record essentially a Mickey & Sylvia production with Tina Turner as guest vocalist. "Sylvia played the lead guitar part while Mickey did the spoken Ag vocals, which Ag would do live. Sylvia also joined the Ag Kets on backing vocals."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 49: "Love is Strange" by Mickey and Sylvia

podcast.title: Pivotal Figure in Hip-Hop
podcast.body: Sylvia Robinson is described as becoming to hip-hop what Sam Phillips was to rock and roll. In 1979, with financing from her husband Joe Robinson's gangster friend Morris Levy, she was more responsible than anyone from the first wave of rock and roll stars for recognizing the commercial potential in hip-hop. "Because Sylvia Robinson, who had been little Sylvia, and the woman calling her lover boy, became to hip-hop, what Sam Phillips was to rock and roll."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 49: "Love is Strange" by Mickey and Sylvia

podcast.title: Possible Co-writer of "It's Gonna Work Out Fine" (as Sylvia McKinney)
podcast.body: Sylvia Robinson (then Sylvia Van Topoele) is possibly the same person as Sylvia McKinney, who is credited as a co-writer on "It's Gonna Work Out Fine," a song Mickey & Sylvia suggested for Ike & Tina Turner. "The other credited co-writer is one Sylvia McKinney, who some sources suggest is the same person as Sylvia Van Topool, who had by this point married Joe Robinson and changed her name to Sylvia Robinson."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Relationship with Joe Robinson and Management
podcast.body: Sylvia started dating Joe Robinson, a man with connections to gangsters, who decided to become her manager to boost her floundering career by forming a duo with Mickey Baker. "But then Sylvia started dating a man named Joe Robinson. Joe Robinson was involved in some way with gangsters."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Unsuccessful Early Recordings
podcast.body: Her initial recordings on Savoy and Jubilee Records were unsuccessful, characterized by a "strange mix of different styles" that lacked a coherent or distinctive sound necessary to establish her as a star. "She had recorded several unsuccessful tracks on Savoy and Jubilee records."
